findings.title: Identification of the area-formula conditional version with the full Gaussian regression at every target is asserted in one sentence
findings.detail: Lines 283-286: 'Integrating its Bayes-weighted tail gives, for each finite evaluation vector, the usual full Gaussian regression at that target. Equality on a countable dense evaluation set identifies the whole C4 kernel.' This is correct: for fixed target v the kernel is the mixture over the tail posterior (density p_{U F_B}(v-Ut)/p_{UF}(v) w.r.t. the tail law, itself Gaussian) of the block fiber Gaussians N(E(t)+E m_B(v-Ut), E Sigma_B^res E^T), which is Gaussian with the regression mean/covariance; equivalently both kernels are continuous in v and agree for a.e. v by uniqueness of disintegration, hence everywhere. The one-sentence form hides the step that makes the equality hold at the specific target 0 rather than almost everywhere, which is exactly the point the paragraph (lines 286-288) is making.

findings.title: Phrasing of the equal-dimensional Sard step
findings.detail: Lines 254-257: 'Area formula applied to its critical set, whose absolute Jacobian is zero, proves that its critical image has Lebesgue measure zero: every image point has at least one critical preimage.' The clause after the colon reads as a claim about all image points; what is meant is that the critical image is by definition the set of coefficient vectors (a,eta) that have at least one critical preimage (p,eta), i.e. for which some critical point in the chart piece is degenerate, and that set is null by L^N(Phi(Crit)) <= integral_{Crit} |J Phi| = 0. The mathematics is correct (I verified the Jacobian identity det DPhi = det Hess F(p)/det B(p) analytically and numerically).

Morse/distinct for the full law gives P(B_(H,H0)>=3)>0 directly, since the C2-neighborhood persistence of the four nondegenerate maxima (lines 487-492) needs only h, not h_*.

findings.title: Physical-mark collapse: the needed input is SG's uniform-in-scale mark-tail bound, not only 'the tight all-mark Gaussian limit'
findings.detail: Lines 572-576 read: 'On A<delta, the base small-bar birth and gap marks have the tight all-mark Gaussian limit in SG/HK; their multiplication by A makes them smaller than delta times a tight variable. First discard the bounded-base-scale O(t^beta) part, then take the base mark-tail cutoff large and delta small.' A limit statement alone does not control the base mark tails uniformly over the logarithmically many base scales s=t/A in (0,s_0) that carry the leading mass. What makes the sketch correct is SG's integrable all-mark majorant (spectral_gaussian_admission/PROOF.md:594-598, 'Its majorant is a^(-1/3)H/(3k^(2/3)), integrable over the full window and all marks ... including tightness of small-a and unbounded birth/gap tails. Far expected counts are O(t).'): it gives E[#{ell<=Ts, |b| or k > R}] <= tau(R) s^beta + C s with tau(R)->0 uniformly in s. I checked that with this bound the error is omega_f(delta R)*O(t^beta log(1/t)) + tau(R)*alpha a^-alpha t^beta log(delta s_0/t) + O(t^beta) (the O(s) far term integrates over A in [t/s_0,delta] against A^(alpha-2)dA to O(t^alpha s_0^(1-alpha))=O(t^beta) at alpha=beta), so the stated order of limits is exactly right. The argument is correct as written for a reader who knows SG's majorant; the one-line pointer would make it self-contained.
findings.fix: After 'tight all-mark Gaussian limit in SG/HK', add 'with its integrable all-mark majorant, which bounds the expected count of window bars with |b| or k above R by tau(R)s^beta+Cs uniformly in the base scale s'.

findings.title: Void marks are not bounded tests; the void rate is obtained from the parent intensity, not from (19)
findings.detail: Line 336-337: 'Nonnegative bounded Borel tests such as window-count/void marks will also be used where their integrals are evaluated directly.' A void indicator corresponds to f=+infinity on the window, which is not a bounded test. In Section 7 the void probability exp(-Lambda_T) (lines 436-439) is in fact computed directly from the Poisson parent rate (24), and window counts enter only through (20), so nothing depends on the phrase; it is a wording slip.
findings.fix: Replace 'window-count/void marks' by 'window-count marks (void probabilities are read off the parent rate (24))'.
